Shared default scope for function-like constructs is defined in src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: export const DEFAULT_SCOPE: string[] = [ "FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction", ]; - require-story-annotation uses shouldProcessNode from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts with DEFAULT_SCOPE and exportPriority, and builds visitors for: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, ArrowFunctionExpression, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, MethodDefinition (src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts). - ArrowFunctionExpression is visited but its type is NOT in DEFAULT_SCOPE, so shouldProcessNode() returns false by default → arrow functions are excluded by default but can be opted into via scope. - require-req-annotation defines visitors in src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts for exactly: - FunctionDeclaration(node) - FunctionExpression(node) (with a guard that skips when parent is MethodDefinition) - MethodDefinition(node) - TSDeclareFunction(node) - TSMethodSignature(node) It uses shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) with the same DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - Tests explicitly exercise this detection set for both rules: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts valid/invalid cases for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, plus explicit tests that unannotated arrow functions are allowed by default. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts valid/invalid cases for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (including anonymous and variable declarators), MethodDefinition (class and object), TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature.,Arrow functions excluded by default (part of REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION): - DEFAULT_SCOPE in src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts does NOT include "ArrowFunctionExpression". - require-story-annotation visitors include ArrowFunctionExpression, but shouldProcessNode() checks scope and thus ignores arrow functions unless they are explicitly added to the scope option. - Tests confirm this behavior: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - Valid: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] valid on arrow function with annotation" (arrow with @story is accepted). - Valid: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default" (unannotated arrow has no error). - In exportPriority tests, "exported arrow function missing @story annotation" is valid when exportPriority is "exported" (showing arrows are not enforced by default).,REQ-JSDOC-PARSING (common parsing strategy for @story / @req): - For @story: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts defines layered helpers: - jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node) uses sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node) and searches for "@story". - commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node) uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node). - leadingCommentsHasStory(node) inspects node.leadingComments. - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node) combines jsdoc, commentsBefore, leadingComments, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory, with a try/catch for robustness. - For @req: src/utils/annotation-checker.ts defines a parallel strategy: - getJsdocComment(sourceCode, node) → sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node). - getLeadingComments(node) and getCommentsBefore(sourceCode, node) collect comments. - combineComments merges leading and prior comments. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix }) then calls hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, all, context, node) (implemented in src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts) and reports via reportMissing if missing. - require-req-annotation: src/utils/annotation-checker.ts checkReqAnnotation() calls reportMissing() when hasReqAnnotation(...) is false; reportMissing() builds a missingReq message with functionName and optional autofix; src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts wires this into visitors for all function-like nodes. - Applies exportPriority === "exported" or "non-exported" to include/exclude nodes. - require-story-annotation (src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts): - Reads options.scope (default DEFAULT_SCOPE) and options.exportPriority (default "all"). -
